A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenRecal research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved from the appendix into the main text.

before.justification: v2 reports original GenRecal benchmark results, component ablations, representation analyses, and dataset-domain experiments, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds autoregressive-loss ablation results and comparative training-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The Recalibrator architecture, three-stage training, autoregressive/KL losses, regularization, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 move from v2 Appendix E into the main text; projection-layer renaming and removal of unused Algorithm 2 inputs do not alter computation.

E1.justification: The training-data mixture, vision-language benchmarks, and MMLU/GPQA/MATH evaluations are retained. v2 Appendix F becomes v3 Appendix E with the same dataset composition and domain analyses. The added experiments use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 6(h–i) adds teacher comparison rows for InternVL2.5-78B, Ovis1.6-Gemma-27B, Qwen3-VL-32B, and InternVL3.5-38B, absent from the corresponding v2 Table 5 panels. The existing distillation comparator set, including ULD and MOT, is retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes reported effective batch sizes from 512/256 to 8192/4096, a substantial training-protocol revision. Table 7 also introduces comparative FLOPs and runtime evaluation. These reported changes do not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds an autoregressive-loss removal ablation for two students across the existing benchmarks (Table 5) and a comparative training-cost analysis (Table 7). These targeted additions extend the retained regularization, depth, positional-embedding, dataset-size, and appendix analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new benchmark averages and runtime measurements do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports averages of 55.0/59.8 without autoregressive loss versus 75.8/77.1 with it. Table 7 adds training times of 18.8, 22.2, and 25.0 hours for GenRecal, ULD, and MOT. Teacher reference scores are added; the earlier benchmark and ablation values are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 and the loss computations are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations appear; the expanded alignment explanations are conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of general-purpose distillation across heterogeneous token types, broad model compatibility, and strong benchmark performance. The additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes distribution matching through KL loss from hard-target supervision through autoregressive loss and interprets the new ablation accordingly. Section 4.4 expands the representation-mismatch explanation and interprets the new cost comparison as supporting competitive training efficiency.

D1.justification: Reported hardware changes from 8 to 128 NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs, while training durations change from days to stage-specific ranges of 2–4, 8–11, and 4–6 hours. Table 7 newly documents ULD/MOT two-epoch budgets and GenRecal stage timings, materially revising resource and reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The Qwen3 technical-report citation is replaced by the distinct Qwen3-VL technical report. Discussion further develops GenRecal’s relationship to ULD and MOT, while the main related-work section and appendix survey remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized revisions move Algorithms 1–3 into the main text, add a projection-layer subsection, reorganize the discussion, and simplify projection terminology. Most introductory, methodological, and appendix prose is retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a narrower single-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning figures and tables. v3 adds Tables 5 and 7 and expands the former Table 5, now Table 6. Existing plotted content is retained, but dense table text becomes smaller.

improvement.justification: The new loss ablation and comparative runtime evidence in Tables 5 and 7 modestly strengthen support for the existing method, while moving algorithms into the main text improves accessibility. These gains are tempered by smaller tables and unexplained hardware/batch-size revisions that are not linked to reruns of the retained results.
